claims.claim: There is an explicit 76-shade implementation of the geometric controller below.
claims.evidence: The source model requires an algorithm tuple (Cl, Init, T), including a transition value for each local-view orbit. The draft supplies only six block cardinalities summing to 76 and informal macro-commands. It never enumerates the shades, assigns meanings to individual shades, specifies the initial colors, or gives the local-view-to-move-and-shade rules. Assigning idle to unlisted views does not repair this because the supposedly listed commands are themselves not defined as views and transitions. Therefore the material below is not an explicit implementation.
claims.witness: The final writeup uses placeholders including "suitable role shades", "bounded controller", "four-stage shift", and "bounded signaled choreography"; no shade/state table or transition table instantiates any of them.
claims.search_method: Direct structural comparison of the authorized draft with the source's formal definition of an algorithm and manual inspection of every controller description in the draft.

claims.claim: The knight invariant supports an adversary-proof row scan and translation.
claims.evidence: Exact integer simulation confirms that the two stated encounter branches are collision-free, avoid edge swaps, and end at the advertised translated K configuration. Enumeration of all 48 signed coordinate symmetries also confirms that the idealized beacon view with a colored neighbor and perpendicular wall has the advertised two-element ±r move orbit. However, the row sweep and bounded two-axis search are not supplied as round-by-round colored local-view rules. In particular, wall-truncated searches, restoration/reorientation of the traveler pair, termination under independently chosen transformations each round, and compatibility of role shades are not proved. The endpoint algebra alone is not a rigorous adversary-proof scan.
claims.search_method: Exact integer branch simulation, 48-symmetry stabilizer-orbit enumeration, and adversarial review of the omitted search and transition rules.

claims.claim: Every non-outer slice is completely scanned, and ordinary slice changes preserve a valid frame.
claims.evidence: The checker confirms the set-theoretic endpoints of both ordinary-transition outcomes: distinct choices produce D(q;d,e,f), while contact followed by the stated rotation produces D(q;e,d,f), without collision or edge swap. It also confirms the relevant idealized two-choice stabilizer orbit. But the draft omits the actual sequences and local rules for forming the penultimate-row pair, finding the diagonal beacon, sweeping the last row, reaching the ordinary-transition staging configurations, and converting D to K. Consequently completeness of every non-outer slice and preservation for every reachable view, including minimum side length four, are not established.
claims.search_method: Exact integer simulation of the advertised ordinary endpoints, signed-symmetry orbit enumeration, and case analysis of the unstated row-boundary and D-to-K procedures.

claims.claim: The outer-corner reset is safe for every symmetry choice.
claims.evidence: Exact simulation of the advertised two edge choices, two x/y choices, and both ±d conversion branches confirms collision-free, swap-free endpoints equal to K(s;y,d,x). The representative first-choice and conversion stabilizer orbits also have the claimed two possibilities. This does not exhaust every execution of a visibility-one controller: the draft gives no colored local-view rules for forming the staging configurations, re-forming the travelers, executing either full line sweep, coordinating followers, or changing shades. Thus it has not shown that intermediate views introduce no additional adversarial branches or conflicting rules.
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of the stated macro-branches, 48 signed-coordinate stabilizer checks, and adversarial inspection of all omitted intermediate transitions.

claims.claim: Every execution perpetually explores every finite grid of side lengths at least four.
claims.evidence: An exact reset-orientation automaton was built from the draft's advertised recurrence. It enumerates all 48 ordered signed frames, all four reset choices per frame, and all vertex boundary/interior categories represented on the 4×4×4 box. Conditional on the premise that each phase covers everything except its far floor face and that both reset lines are swept, it finds no perpetually missed vertex and a maximum of two consecutive missed phases, consistent with coverage by the third phase. The premise and termination of every phase are nevertheless unsupported because Claims 1–3 lack complete transition rules. Without a defined T, the universal quantifier over executions cannot be verified.
claims.search_method: Exact integer state-space search over signed reset frames and vertices, followed by dependency analysis against the missing controller and termination proofs.

target_evidence: The exact target requires either a model-valid ambiguous algorithm for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades whose every execution solves PEP, or a proof that 77 shades are optimal. The draft attempts the first alternative and headlines a full theorem, but it does not define the required shade set, initialization colors, or transition function; several essential operations remain unnamed choreographies or searches. It also gives no 77-shade lower bound. Exact checking supports some macro-level endpoint, symmetry-orbit, and conditional coverage algebra, but this is insufficient to construct or verify an algorithm in the source model. Because the final writeup asserts full target coverage despite that failure, the target is OVERCLAIMED and claimed_resolution FULL is OVERSTATED.
